segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red signal alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
may not proceed on or through any private or public property to enter the intersecting
street
where traffic is not facing a red signal
to avoid the red signal.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head; state in {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady red signal alone is the head displaying circular_red and no other state (no arrow, no flashing state). Same atom as the index maps these words to (NRS_484B_307_8d). It is a device, not a sign or a road feature, so no exclusion applies.

Reuses the index mapping of 'Vehicular traffic facing the signal' (NRS_484B_307_2a). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances'); 'vehicular' limits it to its vehicle members, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'). Facing the signal: the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a carrier c that runs into intersection i at its entrance end (st.lane_enters; c of kind st.travel_region, i of kind st.intersection), and the head governs c or i (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'); governance is control, not a position, as its exclusion requires.

st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; private or public property is ground no highway region covers, so proceeding on or through it is the subject's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) no st.highway region; the 'not a stand-in for the roadway' clause is respected, the test being against the whole way, so a sidewalk or shoulder is not property. The intersecting way is a highway h2 on which intersection i lies (st.on_way: 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there') and on which the approach carrier c does not lie; entering it is the subject's footprint coming to overlap h2 outside i, having overlapped no highway region at the previous observation.

The intersecting street's traffic not facing a red signal is read on that street's approaches into the same intersection: a traffic signal head that governs (dev.governs) a carrier k lying on h2 (st.on_way) and entering i (st.lane_enters; k of kind st.travel_region) displays a state other than circular_red (dev.traffic_signal). The words speak of the signal the street's traffic faces, so the condition reads the device and holds whether or not a road user is on h2.

The purpose 'to avoid the red signal' is read through the conduct it explains: having faced the red on c, the subject reaches h2 without having occupied i (rel.occupies, st.intersection) and without having stood on the property: drv.motion.parked is 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not', at rest throughout a window of min_duration; a road user that parks on the property is there for the property, not passing through it around the signal.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies within the territorial limits of an incorporated city, as the map's reading classifies the area

applicability: The subject is vehicular traffic (ru.aggregate traffic and ru.aggregate vehicle). There are an intersection i, a carrier c of kind st.travel_region that enters i (st.lane_enters c i), and a highway h2 on which i lies (st.on_way i h2) and on which c does not lie, such that: (a) at some observation up to the judged one, the subject occupied c while a traffic signal head governing c or i (dev.governs) displayed circular_red and no other state (steady red alone); (b) at the judged observation a traffic signal head governing some carrier k that lies on h2 and enters i displays a state other than circular_red (the intersecting street's traffic does not face a red signal); (c) the place lies within an incorporated city (asm.within_incorporated_city: the intersecting way is a street); (d) since the latest observation at which (a) held, the subject has at no observation occupied i and has at no observation been parked (drv.motion.parked with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.parking_min_duration): it is passing around the signal, not using the property (purpose read through conduct).
obligation: Re-binding i, c and h2 by the same selection and relations as the applicability (c enters i, i lies on h2, c does not lie on h2, the subject occupied c while a head governing c or i displayed circular_red alone, and has since neither occupied i nor been parked): it is not the case that at the judged observation the subject occupies h2 and does not occupy i while at the previous observation it occupied no st.highway region (it comes onto the intersecting street from private or public property off every public way).

narrowings.why: 'private or public property' is read as ground outside every highway's boundary lines: the subject's footprint overlaps no st.highway region at the observation before it comes onto the intersecting street. A cut across a sidewalk or shoulder alone, which is part of the highway, is not read as proceeding through property.

The purpose of avoiding the red signal is read through conduct: after facing the steady red on the approach, the subject reaches the intersecting street from off the way without having entered the intersection and without having parked on the property.
'Vehicular traffic' facing the signal is read through the vehicle's controlled motion on the approach, whoever or whatever is at the controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject (vehicle, traffic) occupies approach lane c entering intersection i; the head governing c displays circular_red alone; the head governing the cross street's approach lane k (on h2, entering i) displays circular_green. The subject turns right off c into a corner lot, its footprint overlapping no highway region for several observations while moving (never parked), and then comes to occupy h2 outside i. It never occupied i. The place is within an incorporated city.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene: the subject halts on c while its head displays circular_red alone, waits until circular_green, enters i and turns right onto h2 through i; at no observation does it come onto h2 from off the way.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head governing c displays circular_green throughout; the subject passes through i. It never occupied c facing a steady red alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the state of the head governing c is never observed (dev.traffic_signal absent); the subject cuts through the corner lot onto h2.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the subject parks in the corner lot (at rest for longer than the parking duration) before leaving onto h2; while it waited on c facing the red it complied, and after parking the cut-through condition no longer holds.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but every head governing an approach of h2 into i displays circular_red throughout (an all-red interval): the intersecting street's traffic faces red.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of automotive perception and simulator scene-graph sources

param_proposals.name: p.parking_min_duration
param_proposals.convention: the longest halt counted as temporary, as for loading or unloading: a common time limit of a passenger loading zone
param_proposals.source: municipal passenger loading zone time limits

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
A person driving a motorcycle, moped or trimobile or riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
facing the signal
may proceed straight through or turn in the direction opposite that indicated by the green turn arrow
if:

(1) The person stops before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made or, in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, before entering the intersection; (2) The person waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows of the applicable official traffic-control device and the signal does not change because of a malfunction or because the signal failed to detect the presence of the motorcycle, moped, trimobile, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter; (3) No other device at the place prohibits the turn, if applicable; and (4) The person yields
the right-of-way
to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk
and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: 'a signal head; state in {... circular_red, green_arrow(dir) ...}; several states may be displayed at once'. A steady red with a green turn arrow is the head displaying circular_red together with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right (a turn arrow with an opposite turn), and no circular_green, read at the observation of the subject's entry into the intersection, which 'may proceed' fixes.

Reuses the index mapping of the same words (NRS_484B_307_8d). Motorcycle, moped, bicycle, electric bicycle and electric scooter are admitted aggregates for this law and are claimed by id. 'Trimobile' has no applicable definition; ru.motorcycle, 'motor vehicle on two or three wheels ridden astride, including three-wheeled variants', denotes it, used for the undefined word only.

Facing the signal: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier c of kind st.travel_region that runs into intersection i at its entrance end (st.lane_enters), and the head governs c or i (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Governance is control, not a position, as its exclusion requires.

The passage through i (rel.occupies of st.intersection, from entry to exit) is straight through or a turn opposite the arrow exactly when it is neither a turn in the arrow's direction nor a reversal: for green_arrow(left), drv.motion.left_turn_through_region (a heading change 'in the band from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive') does not hold at the exit and drv.motion.u_turn_through_region ('so as to proceed in the opposite direction') does not; for green_arrow(right), the same with drv.motion.right_turn_through_region. The arrow's direction is read from dev.traffic_signal's green_arrow(dir).

(1) Reuses the index mapping of the stop-before words (NRS_484B_307_8a_o1): a stop is drv.motion.complete_halt ('complete cessation from movement', DEF-NRS-484A-255); the marking that indicates where the stop must be made is a st.stop_line ('the transverse line marking where vehicles halt'), the crosswalk a st.crosswalk, each the one recorded as marking the approach carrier's entrance (st.entrance_of, 'exactly that carrier's entrance'), the carrier entering i (st.lane_enters); the side of the mark is read along the carrier's direction (st.lane_direction, prim.region_offset_along), the distance through st.region_geometry, and a halt overlapping the mark or i (rel.occupies) is not before entering it. (2) Reuses the index mapping of the parallel words (NRS_484B_307_8d): the applicable device is the head governing c (dev.governs, st.travel_region); a complete cycle is counted by the display steady red with the green turn arrow coming on again (a rising edge of that dev.traffic_signal state combination) while the subject waits at rest at the place (drv.motion.complete_halt); the signal not changing is the head displaying no circular_green through the wait; the cause (malfunction, non-detection of the subject of its class) is the device's status, read through those displays; the classes named are the subject's own. (3) Reuses the index mapping (NRS_484B_307_8d): another device prohibiting the turn is a dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code', with code no_left_turn or no_right_turn matching the turn, governing c or i; 'if applicable' is where the passage is a turn, drv.motion.left_turn_through_region or drv.motion.right_turn_through_region at the exit; the sign is the condition and the turn is read by the concepts, as the sign's 'not a stand-in for a manoeuvre' clause requires. (4) Reuses the index mapping of '(3) The person yields' (NRS_484B_307_8d): yielding is read in the subject's motion (kin.speed) and in the absence of contact (rel.contact, 'the bodies ... touch or overlap (a collision)').

Reuses the index mappings of 'to pedestrians' and 'lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk' (NRS_484B_307_3a). Pedestrians are the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. An adjacent crosswalk is a st.crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of) of a carrier (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters): a crosswalk of this intersection, tied to it by relations, not distance; within it is rel.occupies.

Reuses the index mappings of 'and to other traffic' and 'lawfully using the intersection' (NRS_484B_307_3a): other road users of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic whose footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies, st.intersection).

operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: precedence where 'direction, speed and proximity' give 'danger of a crash') is not yielded where the subject, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) within the intersection, is on a closest approach to a road user it must yield to within the horizon p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or touches it (rel.contact).

applicability: The subject is of one of the named classes (motorcycle, moped, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregates, or ru.motorcycle for a trimobile). Judged at the observation at which the subject exits an intersection i (its footprint ceases to overlap i, having overlapped it at the previous observation). At the observation of its latest entry into i (footprint came to overlap i, not having overlapped it at the observation before), read by a past operator, it occupied a carrier c entering i (st.lane_enters) governed, as c or as i, by a traffic signal head displaying circular_red together with green_arrow(dir), dir left or right, and no circular_green. The passage is not a turn in the arrow's direction (for dir left, drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(subject, i) does not hold at the exit; for dir right, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region does not) and not a reversal (drv.motion.u_turn_through_region does not hold): it went straight through or turned opposite the arrow. Turn concepts take step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min.
obligation: Re-binding i, c and the head by the same selection (the entry observation's carrier c entering i and its governing head displaying the red with the green arrow), all of: (1) Halt before the entry. Event: the subject's entry into i through c. Place: where a stop line or a crosswalk is recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of), a halt (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) with the subject's body within p.stop_point_tolerance of that mark (st.region_geometry), short of it along c's designated direction (sign of prim.region_offset_along along st.lane_direction) and not overlapping it nor i (rel.occupies); where several such marks mark c, a halt at any of them; where the marks' entrance lists are observed and none marks c, a halt within p.stop_point_tolerance of i's edge at c's entrance end, not overlapping i. History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends only at the approach start (the last observation at which the subject, on a carrier the mark marks, is outside the mark's stopping zone upstream: off it, short of it and farther than p.stop_point_tolerance) or at the subject's previous entry into i; a halt found discharges, either end reached without one violates, reaching neither is unknown; an unobserved association of a mark with c makes the governing mark unknown only where the verdict depends on it. (2) Two cycles: at some observation before the entry since which the subject has not occupied i, the subject was at rest at that place, and since the start of its latest run at rest there the governing head's display circular_red with green_arrow(dir) had risen at least the literal two times (count of rising edges, op ge); unknown where that run's start lies before the recording. (3) At no observation of that run at rest did the head display circular_green (the signal does not change for the subject). (4) Where the passage is a turn (drv.motion.left_turn_through_region or drv.motion.right_turn_through_region at the exit), no dev.regulatory_sign with the code prohibiting that turn (no_left_turn, no_right_turn) governs c or i at the entry. (5) Yield: at every observation from the entry to the exit at which the subject's speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every pedestrian (ru.aggregate pedestrian) occupying a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier entering i, and for every other road user of the traffic aggregate occupying i, the subject is not on a closest approach to it within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), and is not in contact with it (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: The cause of the non-change (malfunction, failure to detect the subject) is the device's operational status, read through its displayed states: two completed cycles at rest at the place with no circular green for the waiting subject.
A complete cycle of the device's lights is counted as the steady red with the green turn arrow coming on again on the governing head while the subject waits at rest at the place.

'lawfully' is not judged by composing the other road users' own rules: the yield is owed to every pedestrian within a crosswalk of the intersection and to every other road user of the traffic aggregate within it.
'driving' and 'riding' are read through the road user's controlled motion, whoever is at the controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle (ru.aggregate motorcycle) occupies approach lane c entering i, with a stop line recorded as marking c; the head governing c displays circular_red with green_arrow(left). The motorcycle halts at the stop line, waits while the red-with-arrow display comes on again once only, then enters i and exits straight ahead (no turn concept holds). No pedestrian or other road user is present.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the motorcycle remains at rest at the stop line while the red-with-arrow display rises twice, the head never displays circular_green, and it then proceeds straight through i. No other road user is in the scene, so the yield is decided on the subject alone.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head governing c displays circular_green at the motorcycle's entry; it proceeds straight through.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the state of the head governing c is never observed (dev.traffic_signal absent).

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the motorcycle already within the stop line's stopping zone on c, moving slowly, under red with green_arrow(left); it enters i and exits straight. No halt is recorded, the approach start and any earlier wait lie before the recording, and no earlier entry into i is recorded.
scenarios.boundary: the motorcycle's approach to the stop line on c and any run at rest there before the recording began

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in permit, but the motorcycle turns right (opposite the left arrow; drv.motion.right_turn_through_region at the exit) while a dev.regulatory_sign with code no_right_turn governs c.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in permit, but a pedestrian occupies the crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of the opposite carrier; the moving motorcycle's closest approach to it lies within the horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1
scenarios.narrative: The head displays circular_red with green_arrow(left) at the motorcycle's entry into i, made without any halt; it changes to circular_green while the motorcycle is in i; it exits straight ahead.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1_outside
scenarios.narrative: The head displays red with the green arrow while the motorcycle approaches, and circular_green from before its entry into i; it proceeds straight without halting.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3
scenarios.narrative: At its entry the motorcycle's footprint overlaps c (governed by the red-with-arrow head) and i; afterwards only i; it did not halt and exits straight.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3_outside
scenarios.narrative: The motorcycle occupied c while c's head showed red with the green arrow, then moved into an adjacent approach lane c2 whose governing head displays circular_green, and entered i from c2 only, exiting straight.

scenarios.name: occasion_s8
scenarios.narrative: As in permit, but for part of the passage a pedestrian occupies a crosswalk of i on a converging course; the moving motorcycle's closest approach to it lies within the horizon below the clearance while the pedestrian is in the crosswalk.

scenarios.name: occasion_s8_outside
scenarios.narrative: As in permit, but a pedestrian occupied a crosswalk of i only before the motorcycle's entry and has left it before the entry; no other road user is present during the passage.

scenarios.name: occasion_s9
scenarios.narrative: As in permit, but for part of the passage another car occupies i on a converging course; the moving motorcycle's closest approach to it lies within the horizon below the clearance.

scenarios.name: occasion_s9_outside
scenarios.narrative: As in permit, but another car occupied i only before the motorcycle's entry and left it before the entry.

onset.justification: The passage begins at the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap i (rel.occupies), not having overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry, the onset each through-region concept states.

occasion.recognition: the observation at which the subject's footprint ceases to overlap the intersection, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit, where the through-region concepts are recognized

under_way.justification: An observation inside the passage is one since the subject's entry into i over which its heading change is being integrated from kin.yaw_rate; before the entry it did not overlap i and no integration has begun.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of automotive perception and simulator scene-graph sources

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: MUTCD stop line placement (4 ft before the crosswalk) plus a placement margin

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (time-to-collision thresholds)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car design dimensions (AASHTO design vehicle P)

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: intersection turning geometry; lane-change heading changes stay well below it

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: intersection turning geometry

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b) [NRS-484B-307-9b],
vehicular traffic facing the signal
may enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow,
but must yield
the right-of-way
to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk
and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.
Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow are thereby advised that so long as the turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: 'several states may be displayed at once'; a steady red with a green turn arrow is the head displaying circular_red with green_arrow(dir), dir in {left, right, u_turn}, and no circular_green, read at the observation of the subject's entry into the intersection, which 'may enter' fixes.

Reuses the index mapping of 'Vehicular traffic facing the signal' (NRS_484B_307_2a): the admitted traffic aggregate limited to its vehicle members (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); facing is occupying (rel.occupies) a carrier c (st.travel_region) entering intersection i (st.lane_enters) governed, as c or as i, by the head (dev.governs, control, not position).

Reuses the index mapping of the parallel words in NRS_484B_307_7a_o1. Entering the intersection is the subject's footprint coming to overlap i (rel.occupies, st.intersection). The movement indicated by green_arrow(dir) (dev.traffic_signal) is the through-region turn concept of that direction recognized at the subject's exit from i: left_turn_through_region for left, right_turn_through_region for right, u_turn_through_region for u_turn; each is the heading change 'between its entry into r and its exit' in the concept's band.

residues.why: An advisory statement to drivers turning with the arrow about the signal phasing opposing traffic faces; it permits, requires or forbids nothing and adds no condition to the duty.

applicability: The subject is vehicular traffic (ru.aggregate traffic and vehicle). Judged at the observation at which the subject exits an intersection i (footprint ceases to overlap i, having overlapped it at the previous observation). At the observation of its latest entry into i (read by a past operator), the subject occupied a carrier c entering i (st.lane_enters) governed, as c or as i, by a traffic signal head displaying circular_red with green_arrow(dir) and no circular_green. Not where NRS_484B_307_9b applies to the subject (exception).
obligation: Re-binding i, c and the head by the same selection (the entry observation's carrier c entering i and its head displaying the red with green_arrow(dir)): the passage through i is the movement the arrow indicates: for dir left, drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(subject, i) holds at the exit; for dir right, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(subject, i); for dir u_turn, drv.motion.u_turn_through_region(subject, i); the concepts take step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min. Unknown where the entry or the integration is unobserved.

narrowings.why: 'vehicular traffic' facing the signal is read through the vehicle's controlled motion on the approach, whoever or whatever is at the controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car (vehicle, traffic) occupies approach lane c entering i; the head governing c displays circular_red with green_arrow(left). The car enters i and exits straight ahead: drv.motion.left_turn_through_region does not hold at its exit.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the car turns left through i: drv.motion.left_turn_through_region holds at its exit.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head governing c displays circular_green alone at the car's entry; it goes straight.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the head's state is never observed (dev.traffic_signal absent).

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle halts at the stop line of c under red with green_arrow(left), waits at rest while that display comes on twice with no circular_green, then proceeds straight through i: NRS_484B_307_9b applies, so the exception holds.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1
scenarios.narrative: The head displays red with green_arrow(left) at the car's entry and changes to circular_red alone while it is in i; the car exits straight.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1_outside
scenarios.narrative: The head displays red with the arrow while the car waits on c and circular_green from before its entry; the car goes straight.

onset.justification: The passage begins at the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap i (rel.occupies), not having overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry, the onset each through-region concept states.

occasion.recognition: the observation at which the subject's footprint ceases to overlap the intersection, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit, where the through-region concepts are recognized

under_way.words: enter the intersection only to make the movement
under_way.justification: An observation inside the passage is one since the subject's entry into i over which its heading change is being integrated from kin.yaw_rate; before the entry it did not overlap i and no integration has begun.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: intersection turning geometry; lane-change heading changes stay well below it

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: intersection turning geometry

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b) [NRS-484B-307-9b],
vehicular traffic facing the signal
may enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow,
but must yield
the right-of-way
to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk
and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.
Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow are thereby advised that so long as the turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: 'several states may be displayed at once'; a steady red with a green turn arrow is the head displaying circular_red with green_arrow(dir) and no circular_green, read at the observation of the subject's entry into the intersection.

Reuses the index mapping of 'Vehicular traffic facing the signal' (NRS_484B_307_2a): traffic aggregate limited to its vehicle members; facing is occupying a carrier c (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters) governed, as c or i, by the head (dev.governs); the yield attaches to the passage the facing traffic makes once its footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies, st.intersection).

Reuses the index mapping of 'must yield' (NRS_484B_307_2a): yielding is read in the subject's motion (kin.speed) and in the absence of contact (rel.contact, 'touch or overlap (a collision)'; not a near miss, which the operationalization bounds).

Reuses the index mappings of 'to pedestrians' and 'lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk' (NRS_484B_307_3a): pedestrians (admitted aggregate) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of) of a carrier (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters): a crosswalk of this intersection, tied by relations, not distance.
Reuses the index mappings of 'and to other traffic' and 'lawfully using the intersection' (NRS_484B_307_3a): other members of the admitted traffic aggregate whose footprint overlaps i.

operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: precedence where 'direction, speed and proximity' give 'danger of a crash') is not yielded where the subject, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) within the intersection, is on a closest approach to a road user it must yield to within the horizon p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or touches it (rel.contact).

residues.why: An advisory statement to drivers turning with the arrow about the signal phasing opposing traffic faces; it permits, requires or forbids nothing and adds no condition to the duty.

applicability: The subject is vehicular traffic (ru.aggregate traffic and vehicle). At the judged observation the subject occupies an intersection i, and at the observation of its latest entry into i (footprint came to overlap i, not having overlapped it at the observation before; read with since), it occupied a carrier c entering i (st.lane_enters) governed, as c or as i, by a traffic signal head displaying circular_red with green_arrow(dir) and no circular_green. Not where NRS_484B_307_9b applies to the subject (exception).
obligation: Re-binding i by the same selection (the intersection the subject occupies, entered from a carrier facing the red with the arrow): where the subject's speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every road user p of the pedestrian aggregate occupying a st.crosswalk recorded (st.entrance_of) as marking the entrance of some carrier entering i (st.lane_enters), and for every other road user t of the traffic aggregate occupying i: it is not the case that the subject and p (or t) are on a closest approach within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject is not in contact with such a road user (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'lawfully' is not judged by composing the other road users' own rules: the yield is owed to every pedestrian within a crosswalk of the intersection and to every other road user of the traffic aggregate within it.
'vehicular traffic' facing the signal is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at the controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car enters i from c under circular_red with green_arrow(left) and turns left while a pedestrian occupies the crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of the carrier it turns across; the moving car's closest approach to the pedestrian lies within the horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the car halts within i (speed at or below the tolerance) until the pedestrian has left the crosswalk, then completes its turn with no closest approach below the clearance and no contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head governing c displays circular_green alone at the car's entry; a pedestrian is in a crosswalk of i.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the subject's speed is not observed (kin.speed absent) while the pedestrian is on a converging course within the crosswalk.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car enters under red with green_arrow(left) and turns left; no pedestrian and no other road user is in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car enters under red with the left arrow; another car occupies i on a converging course; the subject keeps moving with a closest approach within the horizon below the clearance.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of automotive perception and simulator scene-graph sources

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (time-to-collision thresholds)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car design dimensions (AASHTO design vehicle P)

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
Pedestrians
facing such a signal
shall not enter the highway,
unless permitted to proceed by another device as provided in NRS 484B.283 [NRS-484B-283-1d1, NRS-484B-283-1d2, NRS-484B-283-1d3, NRS-484B-283-1d4].

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal: 'several states may be displayed at once'; a steady red with a green turn arrow is a head displaying circular_red with green_arrow(dir) and no circular_green.

'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed by id.

Reuses the index mapping of 'facing such a signal' (NRS_484B_307_2b): the head (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) and the cosine between the pedestrian's heading (kin.heading) and the line from its position to the head is at least p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos. The 'not a stand-in for a stop line or crossing' clause is kept: the head's position is used for facing only.

Reuses the index mapping of 'shall not enter the highway,' (NRS_484B_307_8b): a pedestrian facing the signal already stands on the highway's sidewalk; entering is its footprint coming to overlap (rel.occupies) a st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic', not having overlapped any at the previous observation.

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate pedestrian). At the judged observation some traffic signal head displaying circular_red with green_arrow(dir) and no circular_green lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the subject's position, and the cosine between the subject's heading and the direction from its position to the head's position is at least p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos (the subject faces it). Not where a rule of NRS 484B.283 for pedestrian signals is engaged for the subject (exceptions NRS_484B_283_1d1, NRS_484B_283_1d2, NRS_484B_283_1d3_o1, NRS_484B_283_1d4_o1): where a pedestrian signal governs the crossing, its own rule decides whether the pedestrian may proceed.
obligation: It is not the case that the subject's footprint overlaps some st.roadway region at the judged observation and overlapped no st.roadway region at the previous observation (it enters the roadway).

narrowings.why: A pedestrian facing the signal already stands on the highway (its sidewalk); entering the highway is read as entering the roadway, the part of the highway it is not yet on.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian stands on the sidewalk facing, within reach and within the facing angle, a head displaying circular_red with green_arrow(left); no pedestrian signal is present. The pedestrian steps into the roadway: its footprint comes to overlap a st.roadway region.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the pedestrian remains on the sidewalk while the head displays the red with the arrow.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head the pedestrian faces displays circular_green alone; it steps into the roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the head's position is not observed (dev.position absent), so whether the pedestrian faces it is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a pedestrian signal across the crossing the pedestrian faces displays walk: NRS_484B_283_1d1 is engaged, so the exception holds.

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a vehicular signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: MUTCD far-side signal head placement and pedestrian heading variability

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a vehicular signal head at which the head counts as one the pedestrian faces across the intersection: a wide urban intersection (about 40 m) plus the set-back of a far-side head beyond the far crosswalk
param_proposals.source: urban intersection dimensions and MUTCD far-side head placement

segmentation.text: it is unlawful for any driver
to disobey the instructions of any official traffic-control device
placed in accordance with the provisions of chapters 484A to 484E, inclusive, of NRS,
unless at the time otherwise directed by a police officer.

elements.justification: 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a role, not an aggregate; it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the subject is a road user of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, as the index maps 'the driver' (LVMC_11_16_030).

Nearest atoms only (see the gap): an official traffic-control device governing the subject is a device of these kinds that governs (dev.governs) the travel region the subject occupies; each atom carries the device's state or catalogue code, not the conduct the device instructs, which the corpus states rule by rule (dev.regulatory_sign is 'not a stand-in for a manoeuvre'). The words name no rule, only 'the instructions of any' device.
A device placed in accordance with the chapters is a device present and governing the subject's region (dev.governs): its presence is the evidence of its lawful placement.

Reuses the index mapping of 'unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer' (LVMC_11_40_070): dev.human_direction with role police_officer giving an indication, governing (dev.governs) the travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), at the judged observation ('at the time').

residues.why: NRS 484B.307(11) has no node in the library or in this plan, so the exception it names cannot be composed; where it would apply this node is broader than the law. Reversal: a node for NRS-484B-307-11 is published, and the exception is composed.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate vehicle). At the judged observation an official traffic-control device (a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, regulatory sign or lane control signal) governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies. Not where a rule of NRS 484B.307 is engaged for the subject (exceptions, one per listed node), and not where a dev.human_direction with role police_officer governs the region the subject occupies at that observation (exception).
obligation: The subject complies with the instruction of every such device that governs it: written, once the gap's operator exists, as compliance with every engaged rule that states the instruction an official traffic-control device gives the road user it governs. Not codable with the present formula language: the words name no rule, and no atom carries what a device instructs.

narrowings.why: Lawful placement under the chapters is the device's status, read through its presence governing the subject's region.
'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at the controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies an approach lane governed by a dev.stop_sign and enters the intersection without any halt on the approach; no police officer directs it.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the car halts at the stop line before entering.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No device governs any region the car occupies.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but which regions the stop sign governs is not observed (dev.governs absent).

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a dev.human_direction with role police_officer governing the car's lane indicates proceed: the car passes the stop sign without halting.

gaps.proposal: `compliesWithDeviceRules (subject)`: true at an observation where every rule of the set that states the instruction an official traffic-control device gives the road user it governs, and is engaged for the subject there, is complied with; false where one such engaged rule is violated; unknown otherwise. It decides the action the law requires: what the device governing the road user instructs it to do, which the words leave to the instruction of whatever device governs, naming no rule.
gaps.nearest: Formula.rule (composes one named rule; the words name none, only 'the instructions of any' device); dev.traffic_signal, dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.regulatory_sign, dev.lane_control_signal (each carries a device's state or code, and dev.regulatory_sign is 'not a stand-in for a manoeuvre': none carries the conduct the device instructs)

segmentation.text: Whenever an illuminated flashing red or yellow signal is used in conjunction with an official traffic-control device,
it shall require obedience by vehicular traffic as follows:
When a red lens is illuminated with rapid intermittent flashes,
drivers of vehicles
shall stop before entering the nearest crosswalk in an intersection or at a limit line when marked, or, if none, then before entering the intersection,
and the right to proceed shall be subject to the rules applicable after making a required stop.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal carries the states flashing_red and flashing_yellow of 'a signal head'; an illuminated flashing signal used as an official device is such a head present in the scene; its official status is read from its presence.

'Vehicular traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic limited to its vehicle members, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, as the index maps 'Such vehicular traffic' (NRS_484B_307_5a_o2).

A red lens with rapid intermittent flashes is dev.traffic_signal state flashing_red. It applies to the subject where the head governs (dev.governs) the carrier c (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies) and enters intersection i through (st.lane_enters), or governs i itself.
Reuses the index mapping of 'drivers of vehicles,' (NRS_484B_307_12a): the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; the driver role is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Reuses the index mapping of the parallel stop-before words (NRS_484B_307_8a_o1, NRS_484A_450_2). A stop is drv.motion.complete_halt ('complete cessation from movement', DEF-NRS-484A-255). The limit line is st.stop_line ('the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device'); the nearest crosswalk in the intersection is the st.crosswalk recorded as marking the subject's carrier's entrance (st.entrance_of, 'exactly that carrier's entrance'; the carrier enters i, st.lane_enters). The side of a mark is read along the carrier's direction (st.lane_direction, prim.region_offset_along); the distance through st.region_geometry; a halt overlapping the mark or i (rel.occupies) is not before entering it.

residues.why: The words subject the right to proceed after the stop to 'the rules applicable after making a required stop' without naming any rule of the corpus; this node judges the stop, and the proceeding is judged by those rules on their own terms.

applicability: The subject is vehicular traffic (ru.aggregate traffic and vehicle). Judged at the observation at which the subject enters an intersection i (its footprint comes to overlap i, not having overlapped it at the previous observation) from a carrier c entering i (st.lane_enters) that it occupied at the previous observation, while a traffic signal head governing c or i (dev.governs) displays flashing_red at that entry observation.
obligation: Act before an event (the ontology's approach convention). Event: the subject's entry into i through c. Place: where a stop line or a crosswalk is recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of), a halt (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) with the subject's body within p.stop_point_tolerance of such a mark (st.region_geometry), short of it along c's designated direction (sign of prim.region_offset_along along st.lane_direction) and not overlapping it nor i (rel.occupies); the crosswalk and the limit line are alternatives, and a halt at either discharges; where the marks' entrance lists are observed and neither a crosswalk nor a stop line marks c, a halt within p.stop_point_tolerance of i's edge at c's entrance end, not overlapping i. History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends only at the approach start (the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the mark marks, is outside the mark's stopping zone upstream: off it, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance; for several marks, outside the zone of each and short of each) or at the subject's previous entry into i; never at the recording's start or a distance travelled. A halt found discharges; either end reached without one violates; reaching neither is unknown. The entry is unknown where the observation before it is missing or does not place the subject on a mapped carrier; where a mark's association with c is unobserved, whether it governs is unknown, and the verdict is unknown only where it depends on it.

narrowings.why: 'before entering the nearest crosswalk ... or at a limit line when marked' is read as two alternative places, each marking the subject's approach carrier: a halt within the stop-point tolerance short of either discharges; 'if none' is read where the source's complete entrance lists show neither marks the carrier.
The official status of the flashing signal is read through the head's presence in the scene.
'drivers' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at the controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies approach lane c entering i; a stop line is recorded as marking c; the head governing c displays flashing_red. The car approaches from beyond the stopping zone and enters i without a halt (speed stays above the tolerance).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the car halts with its body within the tolerance short of the stop line, not overlapping it, then enters i.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head governing c displays circular_green when the car enters i.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the head's state is not observed at the entry (dev.traffic_signal absent).

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the car already within the stop line's stopping zone on c, rolling slowly under a flashing red; it enters i. No halt is recorded and no earlier entry into i is recorded.
scenarios.boundary: the car's approach to the stop line on c before the recording began, where a halt may have been made

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The source's entrance lists show no stop line and no crosswalk marking c; the car halts with its body within the tolerance of i's edge, not overlapping i, then enters under flashing red.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of automotive perception and simulator scene-graph sources

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: MUTCD stop line placement (4 ft before the crosswalk) plus a placement margin

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for a driver of a vehicle
to fail or refuse to comply with any signal
of an authorized flagger serving in a traffic control capacity
in a clearly marked area of highway construction or maintenance
or any other area which has been designated as a temporary traffic control zone.

elements.justification: 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion, as the index maps 'The driver of a vehicle' (LVMC_11_20_060_o1).

The flagger's signal is dev.human_direction's 'indication in {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}'. Compliance is read in the subject's motion relative to the flagger's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head', used here as the flagger's place, not as a stop line): the flagger lies ahead of the subject where the vector from kin.position to dev.position has a positive component along kin.heading; passing the flagger is that component turning from positive to not positive. Slowing is read from kin.accel_longitudinal ('acceleration along heading, signed'; not a stand-in for speed); a turn from the heading change integrated from kin.yaw_rate (Term.headingSince).

A flagger is dev.human_direction with role flagger ('a person directing traffic and the direction given'); serving in a traffic control capacity for the subject is the flagger governing (dev.governs) the travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). Governance is control, not a position.

dev.temporary_traffic_control: 'cones, barricades, temporary signs and flashers marking works, a closure or an obstruction'. The area of highway construction or maintenance is a travel region lying on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway) that such a device governs (dev.governs) and the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

dev.zone_sign kind temporary_traffic_control, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road', governing (dev.governs) the travel region the subject occupies: the designated temporary traffic control zone is read from its sign; a sign marking the zone's end ('end' attribute) does not designate it.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate vehicle). At the judged observation the subject occupies a travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.human_direction f with role flagger giving an indication, and r is governed by a dev.temporary_traffic_control device and lies on a highway, or is governed by a dev.zone_sign of kind temporary_traffic_control that does not mark the zone's end.
obligation: Re-binding f by the same selection (the flagger governing the region the subject occupies, in such a zone), with 'ahead' meaning the vector from the subject's kin.position to f's dev.position has a positive component along the subject's kin.heading: (stop) it is not the case that f indicates stop at the judged and at the previous observation, f was ahead of the subject at the previous observation and is not ahead at the judged one (the subject passes a flagger showing stop); (slow) it is not the case that f indicates slow and is ahead of the subject while the subject's kin.accel_longitudinal is at or above p.speed_decrease_decel_min (the subject speeds up toward a flagger showing slow); (turn) it is not the case that the subject passes f (ahead at the previous observation, not ahead at the judged one) while f indicates turn(dir) and the subject's heading change since f's turn(dir) indication last rose (Term.headingSince with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is not a turn toward dir: for left at least p.turn_heading_min to the left, for right at least p.turn_heading_min to the right, for u_turn of magnitude at least p.u_turn_heading_min. A proceed indication requires no further act.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at the controls.
'authorized' and 'serving in a traffic control capacity' are the flagger's status and role, read through the flagger's presence directing the region the subject occupies.
'clearly marked' is read through the presence of temporary traffic control devices governing the region; their clarity is not modelled.
'designated' is read through the presence of a temporary traffic control zone sign governing the region.

Compliance is read per indication: stop as not passing the flagger while the stop holds; slow as not speeding up toward the flagger; turn(dir) as having turned toward dir by the time the subject passes the flagger; proceed as a permission whose non-use is not judged.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies a lane governed by a dev.temporary_traffic_control device and by a flagger (dev.human_direction, role flagger) indicating stop; the flagger is ahead of the car, and the car drives past the flagger's position while the indication stays stop.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the car halts short of the flagger and moves past only after the indication has changed to proceed.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No flagger governs the car's lane; cones mark a work area.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the flagger's indication is not observed (dev.human_direction absent).

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The flagger ahead indicates slow; the car's longitudinal acceleration stays above the threshold as it approaches the flagger.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The flagger indicates turn(left); the car drives straight past the flagger's position with almost no heading change since the indication began.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A person directing traffic with role flagger governs the car's lane but no temporary traffic control device or temporary traffic control zone sign governs it.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_decrease_decel_min
param_proposals.convention: the longitudinal deceleration at or beyond which a sampled acceleration counts as a decrease of speed rather than noise or rolling resistance: the acceleration resolution of the source
param_proposals.source: acceleration resolution of automotive perception and simulator sources

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: intersection turning geometry; lane-change heading changes stay well below it

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: intersection turning geometry

segmentation.text: A school bus
shall not exceed: A speed of 55 miles per hour
when transporting pupils to and from school.

elements.justification: 'School bus' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-230::school_bus, claimed by id and never expanded to ru.school_bus.
kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s: not exceeding the stated speed is kin.speed at or below the literal 55 mph.

Nearest atom only (see the gap): ru.occupant_count, 'the number of persons in or on a vehicle', tells a bus carrying persons from an empty one, but not that the persons are pupils nor that the trip is to or from school; no atom, conduct or feature of the scene carries that service.

applicability: The subject is a school bus (ru.aggregate school_bus) that, at the judged observation, is transporting pupils to or from school (once the gap's atom exists: the bus is in pupil-transport service at that observation).
obligation: The subject's kin.speed at the judged observation is at or below the literal 55 mph.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A school bus in pupil-transport service with twenty occupants travels at a kin.speed of 27 m/s (above 55 mph).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same school bus in pupil-transport service travels at 22 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A school bus returning empty to its depot (occupant count one, not in pupil-transport service) travels at 27 m/s.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A school bus travels at 27 m/s; its occupants are not observed (ru.occupant_count absent) and no service state is recorded.

gaps.proposal: `ru.pupil_transport_service` | a school bus is on a trip carrying pupils to or from a school or a school activity, as the source records the bus's service state (its operator's dispatch record, or a displayed route or destination). **Not a stand-in for:** the number of occupants (`ru.occupant_count`) — a bus may carry persons who are not pupils, or travel empty on a pupil route | local
gaps.nearest: ru.occupant_count ('the number of persons in or on a vehicle': it counts persons, it does not tell pupils from other passengers nor a school trip from another); ru.school_bus (the bus's designation and markings, which it carries whether or not it transports pupils)
